newsitem.title: USA: MGE spring wheat ends mixed, losses limited.
newsitem.headline: MGE spring wheat ends mixed, losses limited.

text.p: MGE spring wheat futures settled mixed, with spillover pressure from CBOT corn and soybeans offset by healthy commercial buying, traders said.

All three U.S. wheat futures markets drew pressure from corn and beans, which closed lower amid forecasts for beneficial rains in key growing areas of the U.S. Midwest. But losses in spring wheat were limited by commercial buying.
"We saw decent scale-down commercial buying, and some of the firms even had to bid up to get stuff bought," a MGE trader said.
Traders said spring wheat was also underpinned by forecasts for rain this weekend in North Dakota.

The state's agricultural statistics service said in its weekly report Monday that some fields in the eastern part of the state were suffering from too much water in fields, and traders said there was concern that more rain would further saturate fields and threaten crops.
MGE spring wheat settled 3-3/4 cents per bushel lower to four cents higher, with Sept down 3-3/4 cents at $3.67.
Traders said Continental bull-spread one million Sept/Dec bushels at three cents. Cargill Investor Services bought 700,000 Sept, and ConAgra was also said to have bought chunks of Sept wheat late.
Traders said activity was mostly light. The MGE estimated Wednesday's volume was 16.466 million bushels.
